subject.title: fix: gateway boots when a configured plugin payload is broken

question: Should Gateway readiness remain green when one enabled configured plugin has an unambiguous, statically verified broken payload and is surfaced as configured-unavailable?
rationale: The patch is a deliberate availability-policy change rather than a mechanical correction: current main’s merged classification fix still refuses readiness, while this branch changes the user-visible contract for monitoring and operators.

options.title: Accept bounded degraded readiness
options.body: Merge the quarantine policy for exact plugin-owned verification failures while retaining fail-closed startup for invalid config, migration failures, missing ownership, and ambiguous verification failures.

options.title: Preserve fail-closed readiness
options.body: Keep the merged diagnostic improvements from the prerequisite PR but do not allow Gateway readiness until every enabled configured plugin payload verifies.

options.title: Defer to a narrower policy proposal
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want a different readiness definition, such as an explicit strict-mode contract or channel-specific handling.

recommendation.title: Accept bounded degraded readiness
recommendation.body: Merge the quarantine policy for exact plugin-owned verification failures while retaining fail-closed startup for invalid config, migration failures, missing ownership, and ambiguous verification failures.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the latest hardening commit and are assigned to the PR, directly connecting them to the remaining readiness-policy decision.
